question: persister
prompt:
Research question: "What measurements or analyses would best reveal why a small fraction of genetically identical cancer cells survive targeted drug treatment?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

Work in two steps. First, in the candidates field, brainstorm 20 candidate ideas, one line each, covering as wide a range as you can. Then select the 5 candidates that best combine being non-obvious with being feasible and informative, and develop those as your ideas.

ideas.title: Barcode-and-rewind lineage tracing
ideas.description: Barcode a cell population, split it before treatment, and profile one half by scRNA-seq while treating the other. Matching barcodes of survivors to their untreated sister cells reveals pre-existing, predictive transcriptional states and shows whether survival is heritable.

ideas.title: Live imaging of signaling dynamics linked to fate
ideas.description: Track single cells with live reporters (ERK/AKT activity, FUCCI cell cycle, apoptosis markers) before and during drug exposure. Retrospective analysis of survivor trajectories shows which dynamic features, such as pulses, rebound or cycle arrest, predict survival.

ideas.title: Fluctuation test with state-switching modeling
ideas.description: Run Luria–Delbrück-style fluctuation assays across many parallel clonal cultures and compare survivor-count variance with stochastic models. This separates rare pre-existing genetic mutations from reversible non-genetic switching and estimates the switching rates.

ideas.title: Single-cell multiome of persisters across drug time course
ideas.description: Profile chromatin accessibility and RNA jointly in the same cells at baseline, during drug exposure and after a drug holiday. This identifies enhancer and transcription factor programs that define the persister state and tests whether they are reversible epigenetic memory.

ideas.title: Pooled CRISPRi/a screen with persister-specific readout
ideas.description: Run genome-wide or targeted CRISPRi/a screens and score survival early under drug, before regrowth, and compare with late resistance outgrowth. Hits specific to persistence, such as chromatin regulators, stress pathways and apoptotic priming, give causal drivers and combination targets.

candidates: Lineage barcoding (e.g., Watermelon/ClonTracer) with sister-cell split before drug to test heritability of survival
Single-cell RNA-seq of barcoded cells pre-treatment, matched to later survivors (Rewind-style) to find predictive pre-existing states
Live-cell time-lapse imaging with reporters for signaling (ERK, AKT) dynamics, then tracking fate under drug
Single-cell multiome (ATAC+RNA) of persisters to identify chromatin-based state switches
Genome-wide CRISPRi/a screen under drug to find regulators of persistence vs. resistance
Single-cell whole-genome sequencing to rule out rare genetic subclones
Mitochondrial mass/membrane potential sorting and survival tracking
Metabolic flux imaging (NAD(P)H/FAD FLIM) of single cells before drug
Cell-cycle state tracking (FUCCI) to test slow-cycling/quiescence correlation
Mathematical modeling of state-switching rates fit to fluctuation-test (Luria–Delbrück) data
Drug-tolerant persister reversal assays: regrow after drug holiday to test reversibility and memory
Proteomics/phosphoproteomics of sorted survivors using low-input mass spec
Spatial transcriptomics of xenografts to link microenvironment niche to survival
Lipid peroxidation/ferroptosis sensitivity profiling of persisters
Single-cell measurement of apoptotic priming via BH3 profiling
Epigenetic inhibitor combination screens during early drug exposure
Stress-response reporters (heat shock, p53, UPR, integrated stress response) pre-drug in single cells
Measuring intracellular drug concentration/efflux heterogeneity with fluorescent drug analogs
Cell size, mass and density measurement (suspended microchannel resonator) vs. survival
Mother-cell inheritance of organelles/protein aggregates and asymmetric division tracking
Transcriptional bursting/noise measurement of key genes using smFISH and live MS2 reporters
